title: Timed guest-ready turnover and final property release
audience: Short-stay turnover cleaners completing a timed turnover and releasing the property.
learningOutcomes: Establish the acceptance criteria and separate what the cleaner approves from what needs coordinator sign-off.
Complete a full timed turnover in a safe order, inspecting from the guest's perspective.
Release the property only after all mandatory checks and approvals are complete.

instruction.heading: Acceptance criteria and approvals
instruction.body: Before you begin, obtain the property-specific checklist, the presentation standard and any guest safety requirements, such as the position of the smoke alarms or the locking of windows the property uses. Read them through once, and ask the coordinator about anything that is unclear. Then sort the items into two groups. The first group is what you can approve yourself, such as the cleanliness of a surface or the number of towels placed. The second group is what needs the coordinator's sign-off, such as a maintenance fault, a missing safety item, a presentation exception or a guest belonging left in the property. A guest-ready property is one that meets the checklist and has every required approval recorded. It is not simply a property that looks tidy. A tidy room with an open safety item is not ready.

instruction.heading: The timed run in a safe order
instruction.body: Start with an authorised entry check and a hazard scan before any cleaning. The hazard scan looks for a gas smell, a damaged cord, water on a floor near a power point, a window that will not lock, and any sign that something is wrong with the property. If you find a hazard, stop and report it, as the safety section explains. Then run the turnover in an order that keeps clean work clean: remove rubbish and used linen, dust from high to low so that dust falls onto surfaces you have not yet cleaned, clean the wet areas with their contact times, work through the kitchen, and finish with the floors. Use the correct tools and follow the product directions for each surface. Plan the run against a time budget, with the contact times and the final inspection built in. For example, a two-bedroom turnover might be split into set blocks for each room, with a block held back for the final inspection. Those figures are examples and the coordinator's standard applies. Never operate an unfamiliar electrical or gas appliance just to show that it works.

instruction.heading: Inspect from the guest's view
instruction.body: Walk in as the guest would. Check the entry, the odour, the lighting, the bedding and its corners, the visible surfaces at eye level and at the edges, the bathroom fixtures, the kitchen, the consumables and the floor edges. Confirm that windows, doors and equipment are in the state the property requires, including any safe state for windows and doors. Record each incomplete or failed item, correct the items that are within your training and scope, and reinspect those items. Report maintenance faults, guest belongings, suspected contamination and stock shortages. Do not hide them to finish early.

instruction.heading: Submit the checklist and release
instruction.body: When the run is complete and the inspection is done, submit the timestamped completion checklist, the authorised photographs, and the exception records and maintenance tickets. Secure the keys and codes as the procedure directs. Mark the property guest-ready only when every mandatory check and every required approval is complete. If the coordinator has not approved an exception, the property is not released, even if the rest of the work is finished. Record the time of release and the name of the person who approved it.

procedure: Obtain the checklist, the presentation standard and any guest safety requirements, and sort the items into what you approve and what needs sign-off.
Carry out the authorised entry check and a hazard scan before any cleaning starts, and stop to report any hazard you find.
Run the turnover in a safe order, with contact times built in, using the correct tools and product directions.
Inspect from the guest's view, and confirm that windows, doors and equipment are in the required safe state.
Record incomplete or failed items, correct those within scope, reinspect, and report faults, belongings and shortages.
Submit the timestamped checklist, photographs and exception records, secure the keys and codes, and release only when approved.

workedExamples.situation: A trainee finishes early, but the final inspection finds hair on bathroom tiles, an empty soap dispenser and an unsecured window.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What do you do with each finding?
workedExamples.reasoning: Record all three with location and time. Correct the tiles and refill the dispenser with an approved product, because both are within scope. Secure the window only if the property procedure permits you to do it. Otherwise, report it to the coordinator. Request a reinspection, and do not mark the property guest-ready until the reinspection is recorded.

workedExamples.situation: After release, a guest reports a hair in the shower and a loose cabinet door, and the checklist was signed as complete.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What do you do with the record?
workedExamples.reasoning: Do not alter the signed record. Add a dated note that the guest has reported the items, and reopen the checklist for reinspection. Report the loose door to the coordinator as a maintenance item and do not attempt the fix unless it is within your scope. Record the reinspection and the outcome, and check the completed checklist against what was actually found.

workedExamples.situation: During the hazard scan, a cleaner notices a faint gas smell near a cooktop.
workedExamples.reasoning: Do not operate the cooktop or any switch, and do not look for the source with a flame. Follow the gas safety steps in the safety section, keep people away from the area, and call the emergency contact in the business procedure. Stop the turnover and record the time and the location. Do not release the property.

equipmentAndPpe: Gloves and approved products for each surface, used with the SDS and the label.
Microfibre cloths and the tools the procedure names for each surface.
Timer and time budget sheet for the run.
Timestamped completion record, camera for authorised photographs, and a key and code log.
Gloves, closed footwear and any other PPE the product SDS and the business procedure set.

commonErrors.error: Marking the property guest-ready before all checks are complete.
commonErrors.prevention: Release only after every mandatory check and approval is recorded.

commonErrors.error: Operating an unfamiliar appliance to show it works.
commonErrors.prevention: Do not operate unfamiliar electrical or gas appliances, and record only what you checked.

commonErrors.error: Hiding a fault to finish early.
commonErrors.prevention: Record every fault and shortage, and request a reinspection.

commonErrors.error: Skipping the hazard scan to save time.
commonErrors.prevention: Complete the hazard scan before any cleaning, and stop if a hazard is found.

commonErrors.error: Ticking the checklist without inspecting the item.
commonErrors.prevention: Inspect each item from the guest's view before ticking it.

commonErrors.error: Cleaning dusty surfaces before the dusting is done.
commonErrors.prevention: Dust from high to low and finish with the floors, so that the work is not undone.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Electrical work in New South Wales. The NSW Government page, last updated 23 June 2026, says that electrical wiring work, including repairing and altering an installation, needs a licence or certificate. Plug-in electrical articles and some low-voltage equipment are outside the definition of an electrical installation. The page does not mention testing or using appliances.

Gas. A cleaner does not operate a gas appliance to test it. Queensland's gas safety guidance says that only a licensed gasfitter can do gas work, which includes installing, altering, repairing, servicing, testing or certifying a gas system, and that a smell which persists after the supply is shut off calls for 000. Victoria's emergency guidance says to avoid switches and flames, ventilate, keep people away, and contact the gas distributor, whose number is set out on the page and varies by area.
This lesson does not grant any gas or electrical licence, and completing it does not certify the function of any appliance.
Release does not create a regulatory certificate. The checklist records what was checked.

qualityStandard: Acceptance criteria and approvals confirmed before the timed run starts.
The timed run completed in a safe order, with the hazard scan first and a guest-perspective inspection at the end.
Faults recorded, and a reinspection requested before release.
Release recorded only when every mandatory check and approval is complete.
documentationEvidence: Timestamped completion checklist with items marked as checked or not inspected.
Authorised photographs, exception records and maintenance tickets.
Release record with the time and the approver's name.
summary: Know the acceptance criteria, and know which approvals you hold and which you do not.
Run the turnover in a safe order, starting with the hazard scan, and inspect from the guest's view.
Record every fault, and release only when every approval is complete.

knowledgeChecks.question: When is a property marked guest-ready?
options: When every mandatory check and required approval is complete
When it looks tidy and the room is presentable to the guest
When the cleaner has finished early and left the property

knowledgeChecks.question: During a timed turnover, should you run an unfamiliar appliance to confirm it works?
options: Yes, to be sure it works before the guest arrives today
No, do not operate unfamiliar electrical or gas appliances
Yes, if the guest asks you to check it when you are done

knowledgeChecks.question: A window is found unsecured during final inspection. What is correct?
options: Leave it, because it is not your problem to fix or report at the time
Hide it from the record so the final check looks clean and complete
Record it, secure it only if permitted, and request reinspection
